acceptance: morize-core exports public Timestamp and TimestampError values from crates/morize-core/src/timestamp.rs.

Timestamp uses one normalized in-memory representation: signed Unix seconds plus subsecond nanoseconds in the inclusive range 0..=999_999_999; the seconds component is the mathematical floor second for negative instants, so each represented instant has one value representation.
Timestamp::from_unix_parts rejects subsecond_nanoseconds >= 1_000_000_000 with TimestampError::NanosecondsOutOfRange { actual } and does not normalize, truncate, wrap, or silently alter input.
Timestamp exposes unix_seconds() and subsecond_nanoseconds() accessors and an associated UNIX_EPOCH value without acquiring the current time.

Timestamp supports Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, and Hash; focused tests confirm ordering across negative pre-epoch values, UNIX_EPOCH, positive values, and adjacent nanosecond boundaries.
Focused tests confirm canonical negative-time semantics, including that (-1, 999_999_999) is exactly one nanosecond before UNIX_EPOCH and orders before (0, 0).
TimestampError is bounded metadata-only and never carries source text, clock/provider state, or platform-specific error payloads.

The implementation defines no now/current clock API, SystemTime conversion, duration arithmetic, timezone/calendar conversion, leap-second policy, Display, FromStr, parser, serde integration, numeric wire encoding, persistence format, migration, or transport mapping.
cargo fmt --all -- --check passes on the exact implementation head.
cargo check --workspace --all-targets --offline passes on the exact implementation head.
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --offline -- -D warnings passes on the exact implementation head.

cargo test --workspace --all-targets --offline passes and includes focused timestamp tests for bounds, normalization convention, negative-time ordering, epoch behavior, value semantics, and Copy behavior.
Cargo manifests and Cargo.lock are unchanged; the Grain admits no runtime, build, or test dependency.
GitHub Actions passes Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows on the exact implementation head before acceptance.

An independent semantic reviewer reviews the exact implementation head for normalized Unix-part semantics, negative-time ordering, bounds validation, absence of clock/calendar/wire behavior, scope containment, and required evidence.
ADR-0004 proof prerequisite for SG-000011 revalidates against the exact WorkPacket baseline before execution.
The implementation changes no path outside crates/morize-core/src/timestamp.rs and crates/morize-core/src/lib.rs.

method.control: Implementation is limited to one dependency-free in-memory Timestamp value/error module, focused tests, and morize-core re-exports. No clock acquisition, calendar/timezone conversion, arithmetic, formatting/parsing, serialization, persistence, transport mapping, or third-party dependency is authorized.
method.review_separation: An independent semantic reviewer must review the exact implementation head for normalized Unix-part semantics, negative-time ordering, bounds validation, absence of clock/calendar/wire behavior, scope containment, and required evidence separately from the implementing agent before acceptance.
method.rollback: Revert the timestamp primitive implementation commits; no persisted format, migration, clock state, or user data depends on this Grain.

minimality.rationale: One standard-library-only two-field timestamp value plus a bounded validation error is the narrowest reusable P1 timestamp contract. It fixes deterministic instant ordering while deferring clock acquisition, calendar/timezone behavior, serialization, persistence, and third-party time libraries.

requirements: Invalid subsecond nanoseconds must fail closed rather than normalize, truncate, wrap, or silently change the represented instant.
No API in this Grain may acquire current wall-clock time or imply clock trust, synchronization, timezone, or distributed-causality semantics.

outcome: morize-core exposes one dependency-free Timestamp value with a unique normalized in-memory instant representation as signed Unix seconds plus a nanosecond fraction, deterministic ordering/value semantics, and strict nanosecond bounds, without adding clocks, timezone/calendar behavior, parsing/formatting, serialization, persistence, transport semantics, or third-party dependencies.
rationale: P1 explicitly requires timestamps, and docs/DATA_MODEL.md requires the first data-model SpecGrains to refine timestamp representation. This Grain defines only a normalized in-memory instant value using signed Unix seconds plus a non-negative nanosecond fraction so ordering is deterministic across pre/post-epoch values while clock acquisition, calendar/timezone conversion, serialization, persistence, and domain timestamps remain separate decisions.

risk.recovery: Revert the timestamp primitive implementation commits; no persisted timestamp format, migration, clock state, or user data has been written by this Grain.

scope_in: Define public Timestamp with private signed Unix-seconds and subsecond-nanoseconds fields using the canonical convention that unix_seconds is the mathematical floor second and subsecond_nanoseconds is in 0..=999_999_999.
Define public bounded TimestampError::NanosecondsOutOfRange { actual } for invalid subsecond values; reject rather than normalize or truncate.
Provide const UNIX_EPOCH, checked from_unix_parts, unix_seconds, and subsecond_nanoseconds while preserving deterministic Clone/Copy/Debug/Eq/Ord/Hash value semantics.

Add standard-library-only focused tests covering epoch, maximum valid nanoseconds, invalid one-billion nanoseconds, negative pre-epoch ordering, adjacent nanosecond boundaries, deterministic equality/hash/order, and Copy behavior.
scope_out: Current-time acquisition, monotonic clocks, SystemTime/Instant conversion, clock trust/synchronization, distributed causality, NTP, or provider/platform clock behavior.
Duration arithmetic, normalization of out-of-range parts, timezone offsets, named timezones, calendars, locale, leap-second interpretation, daylight-saving behavior, or human date/time formatting.

Display/FromStr, parsers, RFC3339/ISO-8601 contracts, serde or other serialization integration, persisted/wire encoding, configuration formats, migrations, storage, APIs, MCP, retrieval, or domain-record integration.
Any third-party runtime, build, or test dependency.
title: Add normalized timestamp primitive
